levels.title: hjkl — Basic Movement
levels.description: In Vim, you never touch the arrow keys. Use h (left), j (down), k (up), l (right) to navigate. The bug below is a single wrong character. Navigate to line 2 with j/k, then to the character with h/l, and fix it with r (replace) or x then i.
levels.hint: The loop should start from 0, not 1. Navigate there with j then l and use r0 to replace.
levels.tests:
import io, sys
_out = io.StringIO()
sys.stdout = _out
count_up(3)
sys.stdout = sys.__stdout__
assert _out.getvalue().strip() == "1\n2\n3"

levels.title: w / b / e — Word Motion
levels.description: w jumps forward one word, b jumps back one word, e jumps to the end of the current word. These are much faster than holding l. Use w to reach the bug and ciw (change inner word) to fix it.
levels.hint: The function returns the wrong operation. Press w to jump to 'subtract' and use ciw then type 'add'.
levels.tests:
assert calculate(3, 2, "add") == 5
assert calculate(10, 4, "sub") == 6
assert calculate(5, 5, "add") == 10

levels.title: 0 / $ / gg / G — Line & File Navigation
levels.description: 0 jumps to the start of the line, $ to the end. gg goes to the top of the file, G to the bottom. A$ puts you at line end in Insert mode. The bug is at the very end of the last line — use G then $ to reach it fast.
levels.hint: Go to the last line with G, jump to end with $, then use r to replace the wrong character.
levels.tests:
assert greet("World") == "Hello, World!"
assert greet("Alice") == "Hello, Alice!"

levels.title: dd / yy / p — Delete, Yank, Paste
levels.description: dd deletes the current line (and copies it). yy yanks (copies) the line. p pastes below, P pastes above. The two lines below are in the wrong order. Use dd on the first line, then p to paste it after the second.
levels.hint: Put your cursor on line 2 (the return line), dd to cut it, move down, then p to paste.
levels.tests:
assert first_last([1, 2, 3]) == (1, 3)
assert first_last([7]) == (7, 7)
assert first_last([]) is None or first_last([]) == (None, None)

levels.title: / — Search & Navigate
levels.description: In Normal mode, / opens a search prompt. Type a pattern and press Enter. n jumps to the next match, N goes back. Use /return to find the return statement, then fix the off-by-one error.
levels.hint: Search for 'n -' with /n - to jump right to the bug. Change n - 1 to n + 1.
levels.tests:
assert factorial(5) == 120
assert factorial(1) == 1
assert sum_to(4) == 10
assert sum_to(1) == 1

levels.title: Fix the Sum
levels.description: sum_list should return the sum of all numbers in a list. It has a subtle initialization bug. Use your Vim skills: gg to go to the top, w to jump to the number, r to replace it.
levels.hint: What should the accumulator start at before adding anything?
levels.tests:
assert sum_list([]) == 0
assert sum_list([1, 2, 3]) == 6
assert sum_list([10]) == 10

levels.title: Count Vowels
levels.description: count_vowels should count all vowels (a, e, i, o, u) in a string. Two vowels are missing. Use /aei to find the string, then A to append at end of line.
levels.hint: There are 5 vowels: a, e, i, o, u. Search for the string and add the missing two.
levels.tests:
assert count_vowels("hello") == 2
assert count_vowels("AEIOU") == 5
assert count_vowels("rhythm") == 0

levels.title: Fix FizzBuzz
levels.description: fizzbuzz returns 'FizzBuzz' for multiples of 15, but the condition order is wrong. Use dd on the first two if-blocks, then p to paste them after the FizzBuzz check.
levels.hint: Check the most specific condition (n % 15) first. Use dd and p to reorder the lines.
levels.tests:
assert fizzbuzz(15) == "FizzBuzz"
assert fizzbuzz(9) == "Fizz"
assert fizzbuzz(10) == "Buzz"
assert fizzbuzz(7) == "7"

levels.title: MinStack
levels.description: A MinStack must support get_min in O(1). The current implementation is O(n). You'll need to rewrite push to store (val, current_min) pairs. Use cc to change whole lines.
levels.hint: Push (val, min(val, current_min)) as a tuple. get_min returns self.stack[-1][1].
levels.tests:
s = MinStack()
s.push(5)
s.push(3)
s.push(7)
assert s.get_min() == 3
s.pop()
assert s.get_min() == 3
s.pop()
assert s.get_min() == 5
assert s.top() == 5
